To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have prepared a series of new coordination polymers based on conformationally flexible chiral imidazole-based dicarboxylic acid anions and that we have carried out preliminary experiments on the use of these compounds as chiral catalysts in the synthesis of α-aminophosponates.
we have synthesized a family of new homochiral coordination compounds with the potential to catalyse asymmetric organic reactions.

the use of chiral imidazole-based dicarboxylic acids as ditopic ligands allows the formation of homochiral coordination networks of different topologies, depending on the metal ion and on the R group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of new coordination polymers based on conformationally flexible homochiral dicarboxylates and the study of their structural and catalytic properties.
the design and synthesis of new chiral coordination polymers and with their application as catalysts.
the synthesis and structural characterization of new homochiral coordination networks of zinc and copper containing conformationally flexible imidazolyl-based dicarboxylic acids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of conformationally flexible ligands in coordination chemistry can be a useful strategy to obtain new and different coordination polymers, but it is difficult to find a suitable application of these compounds as catalysts for the asymmetric synthesis of organic compounds.

, although the chiral 2D zinc and copper coordination polymers obtained in this work were prepared in high yields and with high enantiomeric excesses, the use of these compounds as chiral catalysts in the synthesis of enantiomerically enriched α-aminophosphate esters is not promising.

the conformational flexibility of the ditopic ligands is the key factor to control the coordination modes of the metal centers, which is responsible for the formation of different homochiral 3D coordination polymers, but the presence of a chiral environment around the catalytic center is not enough to induce the enantioselective formation of chiral α-amino acids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the synthesis of new chiral coordination polymers based on conformationally flexible imidazol-4-ium dicarboxylates is possible, but the use of these compounds in asymmetric catalysis has to be further investigated.
, despite the conformational flexibility of the ligands, the coordination polymers are formed by the ligands in a single conformation, which in turn is determined by the metal center.
the use of the chiral imidazole-based ligands [LR]-, in the coordination chemistry of Zn and Cu, afforded homochiral 3D coordination polymers with a very dense crystal packing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to obtain different homochiral coordination architectures from a single chiral ligand.

the conformational flexibility of the [LR]- ligands, together with the different metal coordination preferences of zinc and copper, allowed us to obtain a series of homochiral two-dimensional coordination polymers with different topologies.

the synthesis of chiral coordination polymers with conformationally rigid ligands and the use of these materials as chiral catalysts are more promising approaches to the development of chiral catalytic systems.
